scope.flow: LaunchToken graduation via _graduate/_createPairAndSwapRemaining adding liquidity to a UniSwapV2 (token,quote) pair
scope.environment: Launchpad/LaunchToken contract with UniSwapV2Router addLiquidity and a pre-creatable (token,quote) pair

statements.text: A LaunchToken is near its graduation (approaching BONDING_SUPPLY).
The (token,quote) UniSwapV2 pair can be created by providing the LaunchToken address and quote address, and the attacker can deploy it before graduation.
Attacker makes a direct deposit of 1 wei into the pair and calls sync, bumping the internal reserve of tokenA to 1 wei.
On graduation, _graduate calls _createPairAndSwapRemaining which calls uniV2Router.addLiquidity to add liquidity to the pair.
With reserveA at 1 wei from the attacker's sync, _addLiquidity takes the else path and calls quote, which reverts because reserveB is 0.
The addLiquidity call fails, making the whole graduation transaction revert and disabling graduation permanently.
Permanent DoS: the contract is stopped from performing its main functionality (graduation).
An attacker can make a massive attack by supplying 1 wei of quote to each token made, affecting tokens when they reach BONDING_SUPPLY.
Users will be forced to pull out all of their quote.
When a LaunchToken reaches BONDING_SUPPLY on a buy, graduation should complete by depositing 20% of the token and all held quoteReserve into the UniSwapV2 pool without reverting.
LaunchToken cannot be transferred until graduation and can only be moved by the launchpad and the GTE router; _assertValidRecipient prevents the pair as final recipient.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether the attacker is permissionless/unauthorized; only that an attacker can deploy the pair and deposit.
Timing of pair deployment relative to graduation is described as 'before graduation' but no concrete prior transaction state is given.
Whether the DoS is truly permanent depends on the _assertValidRecipient restriction, which is asserted but not independently verified.
